task1: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at low resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of preserved portal tract architecture, no obvious portal tract expansion, no visible clustering of inflammatory infiltrates within portal areas, and clear separation between portal tracts and surrounding hepatic parenchyma.
task2: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at low resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of preserved interlobular bile duct architecture within portal tracts, no obvious bile duct injury pattern, no widespread duct-centered inflammation, and no apparent bile duct loss or luminal disruption.
task3: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at low resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of preserved interlobular vascular and central venous structures, no obvious vessel-centered inflammatory pattern, no perivenular inflammatory expansion, and no hepatocyte loss around central veins.

task1: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at low resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of only a few portal tracts showing mild inflammatory cell accumulation, preserved portal tract size without obvious expansion, and largely normal spatial organization between portal tracts and surrounding liver parenchyma.
task2: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at low resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of only a small number of interlobular bile ducts showing mild duct-centered inflammatory changes, with overall preservation of bile duct architecture and no extensive bile duct damage across portal tracts.
task3: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at low resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of vasculitic changes involving only a few interlobular vessels or central veins, with limited vessel-centered inflammation and no broad perivenular extension into the surrounding hepatic parenchyma.

task1: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at low resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of inflammatory involvement in most or all portal tracts, visible portal tract expansion, multifocal portal inflammatory aggregates, and a more diffuse portal-based inflammatory pattern across the biopsy.
task2: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at low resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of inflammatory involvement of most interlobular bile ducts, multifocal bile duct-centered injury within portal tracts, and widespread but still recognizable bile duct structures without extensive duct destruction.
task3: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at low resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of vasculitic involvement in most or all interlobular vessels and/or central veins, multifocal vessel-centered inflammatory changes, and focal hepatocyte loss around a small number of central veins.

task1: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at low resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of most or all portal tracts markedly expanded by edema and dense inflammatory infiltrates, with some portal inflammatory areas extending beyond the portal tract boundary into the surrounding hepatic parenchyma.
task2: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at low resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of widespread bile duct injury involving most or all portal tracts, with many bile ducts showing degenerative alteration, distorted duct profiles, and focal destruction or collapse of the bile duct lumen.
task3: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at low resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of severe central venous inflammation and perivenular inflammation, with inflammatory extension from central veins into the surrounding hepatic parenchyma and broad areas of pericentral hepatocyte necrosis.

task1: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at high resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of portal tracts showing only rare scattered resident inflammatory cells, absence of obvious lymphocytic or mixed inflammatory cell infiltration, no portal edema, and no inflammatory extension into adjacent hepatic parenchyma.
task2: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at high resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of intact interlobular bile duct epithelium, absence of intraepithelial inflammatory cell infiltration, preserved epithelial polarity, uniform epithelial nuclei, no cytoplasmic vacuolization, and no bile duct degenerative change.
task3: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at high resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of intact endothelial lining in interlobular arteries, interlobular veins, and central veins, absence of subendothelial inflammatory cell infiltration, no endothelialitis, and no perivenular hepatocyte injury or necrosis.

task1: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at high resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of sparse lymphocytes and other inflammatory cells within a small number of portal tracts, minimal portal inflammatory infiltration, no marked portal edema, and no obvious spillover of inflammatory cells into the adjacent hepatic parenchyma.
task2: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at high resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of mild inflammatory cell infiltration within the epithelium of a few interlobular bile ducts, slight bile duct epithelial injury, enlarged epithelial nuclei, and increased nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio.
task3: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at high resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of mild endothelialitis in a small number of interlobular arteries, interlobular veins, or central veins, with focal subendothelial inflammatory cell infiltration and minimal endothelial-associated inflammatory damage.

task1: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at high resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of mixed inflammatory cell infiltration in most or all portal tracts, including lymphocytes, plasma cells, scattered neutrophils, and eosinophils, with portal tract expansion; in some areas, numerous eosinophils may be accompanied by portal edema and swollen microvascular endothelial cells.
task2: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at high resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of inflammatory cell infiltration within the epithelium of most bile ducts, frequent bile duct epithelial injury, nuclear pleomorphism, epithelial polarity disorder, and cytoplasmic vacuolization in many duct epithelial cells.
task3: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at high resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of endothelialitis involving most or all interlobular arteries, interlobular veins, and/or central veins, with clear subendothelial inflammatory cell infiltration, endothelial-associated inflammation, and focal pericentral hepatocyte loss around some central veins.

task1: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at high resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of dense mixed inflammatory cell infiltration composed of lymphocytes, plasma cells, neutrophils, and eosinophils, marked portal edema, severe portal tract expansion, and inflammatory cells breaching the limiting plate and extending into adjacent liver tissue.
task2: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at high resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of severe bile duct epithelial inflammation and injury, with most or all bile ducts showing degenerative changes, marked epithelial disorganization, focal bile duct luminal destruction, and collapse or fragmentation of duct epithelial structures.
task3: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at high resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of moderate to severe central venulitis and perivenulitis, dense inflammatory cell infiltration beneath and around the venous endothelium, extension of inflammation into adjacent hepatic parenchyma, and necrosis of many hepatocytes around central veins.
